task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The observable field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so literal field search is not sufficient.

The byte-plan input is prepared only after valid batch-key entry, attested profile selection, non-plain codec selection, non-default shard selection, normalization opt-in, scan, preview, explicit consent, seal and final commit gate have all succeeded.
The active function is surrounded by high-similarity ticket reducers and 44 off-chain decoy modules.

The target path crosses delegated event handling, action-table routing, scan-state mutation, preview-state mutation, consent/profile/codec/shard gating, seal-state mutation, final gate verification, expanded form normalization, tuple packing, byte-plan preparation, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, middleware, state-machine transit calculation and sink wrapping.
Submit-time debug and info decoys emit byte-like shadow keys that do not feed the requested byte_array_payload field.
The same core module retains legacy reducer factories that resemble the target constructor but do not construct the byte-array payload.
Form fields are collected only after the multi-action gate opens, then transformed after Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and CustomEvent boundaries.
The final sink receives an already encoded byte-array payload under a dynamically reconstructed field name.
Route action context surrounds the byte-array construction, while the sink stays outside the transformation.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is derived from prepared upload form fields transformed through byte-array mixing rather than from environment digesting, request signing, UI state encoding or request payload rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output has no request proof or token semantics and no network request is made.
The form and route state are path context; the target value is anchored by byte-array conversion and payload construction.
No request body is emitted or rewritten.
